title: Hungary Bets on Wealth Tax and Euro Ambitions to Rebuild Fiscal Credibility · 16 Oct
keywords: Hungary, wealth tax, euro adoption, fiscal deficit, ERM II, Hungarian forint, EU convergence criteria, Budapest, austerity, European Union, Hungarian National Bank, public finances, Central Europe
notes: Hungary's new government is pursuing a sweeping fiscal overhaul, combining a proposed wealth tax on its richest households with a long-range target to adopt the euro by 2032. Both moves are designed to signal a break with the past, but analysts and critics warn the plans face formidable practical obstacles. The central test is whether Budapest can close a budget deficit projected at roughly 7.5 percent of GDP while persuading citizens and Brussels that the burden is being shared fairly.
